title: Updated my game after a while
author: Leather_Tomorrow4993
selftext:
Hey everyone,

while ago I posted this Subway surfers clone created with AI thanks to Pixelfork and threejs. Today I found time and added some things to make it more fun. Appreciate any feedbacks. 

Playable link: https://www.pixelfork.ai/publish/7df95317-7c6c-4c50-b8cd-adfe2046570c

I used ready ready-made assets mainly from poly.pizza and itch.io

comments.author: ineedthealgorithm
comments.body: Wow, this is actually very impressive. Would love to know the workflow. Could you share it, please?

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: Good on you for putting something together. But did you learn anything from the experience? I'm also asking why anyone would play something of this genre.

replies.author: PuteMorte
replies.body: Is this the magic school bus sub or what

replies.author: DocHolidayPhD
replies.body: From a game dev perspective, I see about a hundred of these clones every month, so the market is flooded (and marketing is a later stage of game dev worth considering). So what is the differentiator for this version of subway surfers that makes it worth playing. I'm not a fan of the original game, so I don't know what sets this game apart as unique or better. Having learned from the experience is also a plus, given an AI agent could likely have created this with minimal prompting. All of this is relevant because If you took nothing away from the experience and had an algorithm throw together something that is undifferentiated, then what was the point of the experience?

replies.author: PuteMorte
replies.body: Respectfully said, your perspective is out of touch with AI and what it provides. Game development is currently evolving into a democratized activity. It doesn't have to either be a useful learning experience or a profitable one.

replies.author: DocHolidayPhD
replies.body: My perspective is absolutely in line with AI and what it provides. I'm saying the experience has to yield something other than the game as the outcome. Otherwise you are objectively wasting time and resources. What was the outcome besides the game itself is my question. Sure you can have an agent throw together a game like this with some prompting, but even then, at minimum the outcome besides the game may be exploring what AI agents are capable of and in that case you have learned what you can do with an AI agent.

replies.author: PuteMorte
replies.body:
>objectively wasting time and resources

We are talking about **game** development here. You would think a "game developer" understands the concept of ludicity.

replies.author: DocHolidayPhD
replies.body: Most play is motivated by something, often by learning. Learning is arguably the foremost motivation to play evolutionarily speaking. We play to learn rules, concepts, limits, how to manipulate and break things. It's no different with game development than any other thing.
